blocks.text: These are the names of the unclean birds, both those found in Scripture and those which the masters of the Jews put forward from tradition. To draw up a list of them was easy for Maimonides; but he did not even attempt to interpret them, which is what we expected from such a teacher. And, what is more surprising, the Talmudic doctors, older by so many centuries, explain only a few, and those very ambiguously, so that they plainly grope in sheer darkness. That the Greek translators too, who lived as long before most of the Talmudists as these did before Maimonides, were often at a loss here is shown by how little they agree with themselves, and by how they pull the name of a single bird into such different meanings. For in the Babylonian captivity the Jews partly forgot their language, and the purity of Hebrew degenerated into Syriac. Hence, after the return from that captivity, the true meaning of some words whose use was rarer was lost. Among these were certain names of birds. Hence Aben Ezra on Levit. XI, 29. 30., where Moses forbids eight kinds of creeping things: גם אלה השמנה לא נוכל לדעתם גם העופות כי אם מדברי קבלה, Neither these eight (creeping things), nor the birds either, can we truly know, except from the words of tradition. But this tradition is nowhere extant. And the authors of the traditions, the Talmudists, send us elsewhere, namely to skilled fowlers. Thus in [III, 122] Cholin fol. 63b: א״ר יצחק עוף טהור יאכל במסורת נאמן הצייד לומר עוף זה טהור מסר לי רבי א״ר יוחנן והוא שבקי בהן ובשמותיהן, R. Isaac said: A clean bird is eaten on the tradition of a trustworthy fowler, so that you may say, This bird is clean, as my master (the fowler) handed down to me. R. Iochanan: Provided he is experienced in them and in their names. Hence Maimonides, in the place cited above, section 15: כל מי שהוא בקי במינין אלו ובשמותיהן ה״ז אוכל כל עוף שאינו מהם ואינו צריך בדיקה ועוף טהור נאכל במסורת והוא שיהיה דבר פשוט באותו מקום שזה [col. 355] עוף טהור ונאמן צייד לומר עוף זה התיר לי רבי הצייד והוא שיוחזק אותו צייד שהוא בקי במינין אלו ובשמותיהן Whoever is practised in those species (which are forbidden) and in their names may freely eat all those birds which are not in that list, and needs no further examination. And a clean bird is eaten on tradition, when it is clearly established in the place where it is that it is a clean bird; and there a fowler is trustworthy, so that (the one who eats) may say, My master the fowler permitted this bird to me. That is, provided that fowler is confirmed to be practised in those species and in their names. But since fowlers of this kind are nowhere to be found, he adds in section 16: מי שאינו מכירן ואינו יודע שמותיהן בודק בסימנין אלו שנתנו חכמים כל עוף שהוא דורס ואוכל בידוע שהוא מאלו המינין וטמא ושאינו דורס ואוכל אם יש בו אחד משלשה סימנין אלו ה״ז עוף טהור ואלו הן אצבע יתירה או זקף והיא המוראה או שהיה קרקבנו נקלף ביד He who does not know those birds and does not know their names distinguishes them by these signs which the sages have handed down to us. Every bird which tears its prey by trampling on it and devours it is evidently of those species and is held unclean. But a bird which is not rapacious and carnivorous is held clean if one of these three signs is found in it: namely, 1. if it has a superfluous toe (that is, a spur, as in cocks); 2. or a crop, which in Hebrew is called murea; 3. or if its gizzard can be stripped by hand (without a knife). These are taken partly from the Talmudic tractate Cholin, partly from the Chaldee paraphrase of Jonathan, which reads thus at Levit. XI, 13.: וית אלין מיניא תשקצון מן עופא דלית להון ציבעא יתירא ודלית זקפתא ודקורקבניה ליתוהי מקליף, And these species among the birds you shall detest: those which have no superfluous toe, and which have no crop, and whose gizzard is not stripped. This last I do not well understand. Yet the Geonim make so much of this last sign that, if this one alone is lacking in a bird, they never permit it to be eaten, as Maimonides explains at length. But let whoever is curious about such trifles consult the cooks of the Jews.
